items.title: SN 1100: Booby Trapping LLMs - AI Frenzy in Cybercrime
items.author: feedmail@twit.tv (TWiT Editors)
items.content:
Think your open-source AI model is safe? This episode uncovers how LLMs can be secretly booby-trapped with undetectable backdoors, raising the stakes for anyone deploying AI in serious environments.

  • Anthropic cuts live Internet access during testing.
  • Will LLM technology turn out to be an uncontrollable dead end?
  • What alternative AI technologies are underway?
  • Anthropic offers free AI vulnerability scanning for open source.
  • South Korean banks hit by Claude-driven cyberattacks.
  • Japan declares a state of cyber-emergency due to attacks.
  • For one listener, agentic coding has taken the joy out of coding.
  • A listener is having way too much fun with AI and Halloween.
  • Some listeners believe I'm downplaying the dangers of AI.
  • We carefully examine the consequences of maliciously trained AI

items.title: SN 1099: An Alien Mind - From RSA Weakness to Agentic Attacks
items.author: feedmail@twit.tv (TWiT Editors)
items.content:
As AI becomes startlingly capable, top minds at OpenAI admit they can't always control what their own creations do—or even fully understand how they think. This episode dives into the real-world tension between rapid progress and the growing challenge of keeping AI truly aligned.

  • GLM-5.3 can be and has been abliterated. What does that mean?
  • Firefox 157 repairs a large number of high-impact vulnerabilities.
  • A surprising reduction in RSA crypto strength has been discovered.
  • Powerful agentic AI is being used to attack merchants.
  • A new and potent Spectre-style processor attack has been designed.
  • A neighbor falls victim to a Bitcoin scam. What can be done?
  • A new and surprising use was found for GRC's DNS Benchmark.
  • An examination of the growing alignment challenges created by more intelligent AI

items.title: SN 1098: How worried should we be? - Unpredictable Agents
items.author: feedmail@twit.tv (TWiT Editors)
items.content:
With millions racing to embrace AI assistants and cybercriminals pivoting to new, high-stakes tactics, the episode tackles the dizzying pace of change and asks: just how worried should we be? The discussion pulls back the curtain on AI's unpredictable power, the escalation of digital extortion, and why the next breach may hit closer to home than you think.

  • The regularity of "Irregular"
  • More rogue OpenAI breaches
  • The Seven Deadly Sins (TSDS) hacker group
  • Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) cargo ship hacked
  • The FBI offended ShinyHunters's delicate sensibilities
  • Canonical switches to an every–2-weeks release cadence
  • Axios' AI 101: AI Explainer for normal people
  • How worried should we be?

items.title: SN 1097: Mega Patch Tuesday Fallout - When AI Outsmarts Its Makers
items.author: feedmail@twit.tv (TWiT Editors)
items.content:
After Microsoft's historic Mega Patch Tuesday, enterprise IT teams worldwide are scrambling as a wave of updates triggers system meltdowns, broken domains, and silent Excel failures. Find out how AI-driven speed collided with real-world chaos.

  • Andrew Ng weighs-in on AI Doomsaying.
  • The wisdom of outsourcing AI security testing.
  • The true risk of an AI-created bioweapon.
  • The EU KIDS Act -- this one is even messier.
  • "Nightmare Eclipse" finally unmasks himself.
  • A whitehat firm used Claude to attack OpenAI.
  • Cisco's own massive 77 CVE update.
  • What was the fallout from Sept's Patch Tuesday
